title: STP-RAG

lines: A feasibility, requirements, and evidence-led project presentation
Mohammad Sameer • Rajeev Kumar Gupta • Mohit Dev Tomar
Department of Computer Science and Engineering
Sharda School of Computing Science and Engineering, Sharda University

notes: Introduce the project in one sentence: we study how chunk boundaries and selectively attached context change evidence retrieval and answer quality. This deck follows the uploaded Evaluation 1 rubric; it is not a claim that every implementation detail has already been independently verified.

title: What this evaluation should establish

lines: Focus: a justified project plan and specification—not only model accuracy.

notes: The rubric contains eight five-mark categories plus ten guide marks: fifty in total. Spend most of the talk demonstrating feasibility, objectives, constraints, requirement traceability, and accountability. Communication is assessed throughout. Do not imply that this slide guarantees marks.

title: The problem: a correct statement can lose its context

lines: The problem: a correct statement can lose its context
Background: Lewis et al., 2020; Chen et al., 2024. Toy example—not benchmark evidence.
Question: Which calibration factor applies to sensor A?
Chunk 2: “Apply this factor only to sensor A.”
Risk: a retrieved chunk may be relevant
Research question: when do transition signals and selected context help—and when do they hurt?

notes: Explain the example without calling it an experimental result. The example only illustrates the dependency problem. Avoid saying that STP necessarily produces this boundary or always recovers the right context. Existing RAG and granularity work motivate the problem; the proposed focus is reuse of a transition profile across representation decisions.

title: System architecture: representation first, retrieval second

lines: System architecture: representation first, retrieval second
Dev calibration → frozen parameters; no test-set tuning
Core scope: document segmentation, context attachment and controlled comparison.
Not evaluated here: a separate evidence-sufficiency or secondary-retrieval controller.

notes: Explain v as local semantic displacement, a as change in that displacement, and sigma as local variability. The same profile is reused for representation decisions. Encoder revision and index backend are not confirmed in the supplied experiment record, so do not name a particular encoder or vector database as measured fact. Context ON/OFF is an ablation, not a second retrieval stage.

title: Validation plan: isolate components rather than add everything

lines: Validation plan: isolate components rather than add everything
Study design and run count: supplied implementation walkthrough. Dataset sources: Yang et al., 2018; Dasigi et al., 2021.
6 arms × 3 seeds × 2 datasets = 36 reported runs. Raw-run verification remains open.

notes: Show how each arm answers an objective. Full STP versus velocity-only is not a clean structure-only or volatility-only test; those isolated controls are still absent. Dataset sample counts, retrieval setting and metric mappings must be supplied before making benchmark-wide claims.

title: Preliminary evidence: context helps one dataset, hurts another
category: Feasibility evidence | not a universal performance claim

lines: FEASIBILITY EVIDENCE | NOT A UNIVERSAL PERFORMANCE CLAIM
Preliminary evidence: context helps one dataset, hurts another
Source: supplied aggregate tables; means across three seeds. Four selected arms shown; all six appear in backup slide 15.
Fixed-size leads; context drops F1 by 0.037.

notes: These are reported aggregate means, not rerun results. HotpotQA F1 increases from 0.344 to 0.410 versus velocity-only; against STP without context the gain is 0.127. QASPER F1 drops from 0.105 to 0.068 with context, and fixed-size is best overall in the supplied table. This is why feasibility and novelty should not be defended using a universal superiority claim. No significance or energy/cost claim follows from this figure.

title: Evaluation 1 takeaway

lines: Transition-guided chunking and context, evaluated against simple baselines.
Mixed results: context helps HotpotQA but reduces QASPER answer F1.
Make the experiment record auditable and close the requirement-verification gaps.
Guide feedback sought: scope • acceptance criteria • responsibilities • realistic milestones

notes: Close with what has been specified, what the preliminary data show, and what remains to be verified. Invite guide feedback on the requirement specification and feasibility constraints, rather than merely asking whether the result number is good. Use the two backup slides only if needed.

title: Backup: all six ablation arms

lines: Source: supplied HotpotQA and QASPER aggregate results. Rounded means only; three reported seeds.
No claim of statistical significance: paired predictions and bootstrap details still require verification.

notes: Use this table to avoid selective reporting. Higher recall is not the same as a better answer. Full STP does not reduce QASPER chunk count: it creates more chunks than velocity-only. If asked about p-values or the very narrow reported confidence intervals, state that the underlying bootstrap record must be audited.
